title: To Our Almighty Maker, God
description: To Our Almighty Maker, God in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 98, part 1, headed “Praise for the gospel”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To our al-might-y Mak-er, God, New hon-ours be ad-dress'd; his great sal-va-tion shines a-broad, And makes the na-tions blest.

lines: He spake the word to Abraham first,
The Gentiles make his Name their trust,
Let the whole earth his love proclaim
And spread the honours of his Name

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
